content:
zoe: Following the midnight postmortem: recurring throughput backpressure on dedicated pools. Proposal: update Dedicated tier SLOs — latency p95 target relaxed from 250ms -> 320ms, and add an explicit throughput SLO of 800 rps steady-state (previously unspecified). Rationale: new batching changes increase amortized token latency during peak sustained tails.

rahul: Can you share the numbers from the 14d window you used? Also want the errorbudget impact calc.

zoe: 14d window. Observed median p95=280ms, incident window p95 spikes up to 480ms at 95th percentile of days. Sustained throughput flattened at ~820 rps causing queuing. Errorbudget impact: if we keep old SLO, projected monthly burn ~28%. With proposed targets projected burn ~6-9%.

mica: Who will own the throughput SLO enforcement? We need a capacity throttle + autoscaler policy tie-in.

zoe: Proposal: infra-team (rahul) to own autoscaler policy changes, eng-sre (mica) to own alerts and dashboard SLIs, eng-platform (tony) to publish the SLA blurb and route config. Timeline: policy changes in 2 business days, observability updates within 48h, verification for 5 days.

ton y: I'll add a per-pool throughput trend and a burn-rate indicator. Also will create a per-GPU saturation panel.

mica: For alerting, prefer a composite alert: sustained p95 breach OR throughput drop of >15% for 3m triggers page. No noisy short spikes. Pseudo-rule below.

```
alert: Dedicated_Throughput_SLO_Breach
expr: (increase(dedicated_request_duration_seconds_bucket{le=\"0.32\"}[5m]) / increase(dedicated_requests_total[5m]) < 0.97)
  or (rate(dedicated_rps[3m]) < 0.85 * avg_over_time(dedicated_rps[1h]))
for: 5m
labels: {severity: "page", team: "infra"}
annotations: {runbook: \"/runbooks/dedicated-throughput\"}
```

natalie: I'll coordinate the customer-facing wording. We should avoid phrasing that sounds like degraded service; frame as "updated performance window to reflect new batching optimizations." Legal review required.

devops-bot: Incident #2025-044 followups assigned: rahul (autoscaler policy), mica (alerts + verification), tony (dashboards + SLA draft). See /incidents/2025-044/followups.

rahul: I'll land a conservative autoscaler tweak: 2x burst headroom, queue limit clamp at 2500, and a rollback flag if errorbudget burn jumps >12% in 24h. Canary plan: region eu-west first at 10% traffic, then 40%, then 100% across 36h.

mica: I'll implement verification harness: daily synthetic load that ramps to 900 rps for 15m and records p50/p95/p99 + token loss rate. If token loss >0.2% we abort.

zoe: Added one more constraint: do not change customer-facing SLA on the hosted tier — this is Dedicated-only. Natalie: please ensure product page note says Dedicated SLO update and includes link to incident.

tony: Dashboard PR: https://git.internal/r/dashboards/pulls/614 — includes throughput SLO panel, burn-rate sparkline, and autoscaler metrics.

rahul: Autoscaler PR: https://git.internal/r/infra/pulls/212 — includes canary rollout script and rollback monitor.

mica: Alert PR: https://git.internal/r/alerts/pulls/319 — includes composite rule and silence policy for short spikes.

zoe: Action items recap:
- rahul: implement autoscaler + canary (due +2 days)
- mica: alerts, verification harness, daily checks (start after canary)
- tony: dashboards + SLA note draft (due +1 day)
- natalie: product/legal wording and publish (due +3 days)

Please post progress here. Small updates only. :thumbsup:

devops-bot: Followup checklist updated: https://incidents.internal/2025-044/followups.

rahul: Canary 10% -> initial metrics at 3h: p95=300ms, throughput=790 rps, queue depth nominal. No rollback triggers.

mica: Running synthetic ramp now. Early result: token loss 0.05%, p99 at 620ms under ramp but p95 within target.

zoe: Good. Keep monitoring for the 5-day window. If sustained burn estimate creeps >10% we'll revert fixes and open a follow-up incident.

mica: 48h checkpoint: cumulative errorbudget burn projected at 7%. Autoscaler behavior looks stable. Scheduling full roll to 100% tonight.

natalie: Draft SLA blurb posted: https://product.internal/sla/notes/dedicated-2025-044 — legal looped in.

rahul: Rolling to 100% now. Will keep the rollback monitor active for 24h.

zoe: Thanks team. If we see the recurring pattern again (roughly cadence every 5-7 weeks per incident history), we'll prioritize a memory/batching optimization sprint. Closing thread after 7-day verification completes."
